title: Soft-commit lanes and graceful overage mitigation for Dedicated
creator: Marco Alvarez
description: Add a 'soft-commit lanes' feature to Redwood Dedicated to allow short-lived, low-latency capacity commitments drawn from a shared surge pool with graceful overage mitigation and customer-visible accounting. This ticket designs and implements: (1) the soft-commit allocation algorithm (time-decay leases + optimistic allocation), (2) autoscaling integration and policy hooks, (3) billing smoothing and overage cap windows, and (4) Console UX and alerts for tenant usage and forecasts. Goal is to reduce throttling during short spikes while preventing bill surprises and preserving baseline throughput guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: Soft-commit lanes implemented server-side: API to request temporary commits with TTL and priority weight
Lease decay policy implemented: committed capacity auto-reclaims after TTL with exponential backoff attempts before hard reclaim
Autoscaler integration: Node pool autoscaler respects soft-commit pressure signals and can trigger fast-path scale-up within configured burst budget
Billing pipeline emits per-tenant soft-commit usage events and applies smoothing window (configurable 1h default) to reduce instant overage charges
Console surfaces a soft-commit usage panel, current burst budget, and projected cost impact for next 1h
Canary rollout plan executed for 5 tenants, no regressions to SLOs (p95 latency) and no invoice disputes in test tenants
implementation_notes: We will model soft-commit as a lightweight lease object attached to tenant allocations; leases carry: requested_rps, ttl_seconds, priority, origin (api/console/autoscaler)

Allocation algorithm: optimistic grant up to min(shared_pool_remaining, requested_rps) and attach a decay timer. If pool contention later occurs, leases with lower priority or older age are trimmed first.
Autoscaler hooks: expose 'soft_commit_pressure' metric aggregated per-fleet; autoscaler policy 'aggressive-burst' will scale nodes faster but deduct from tenant burst budget.

Billing: emit 'soft_commit_event' to billing-stream with fields: tenant_id, seconds_granted, rps_granted, smoothing_window. Billing job will compute amortized cost over smoothing_window to avoid immediate overage spikes.
Safety: hard guardrails enforce tenant-level burst caps and global protective floor to preserve baseline reserved throughput.
Telemetry: dashboards for pool utilization, lease churn, reclaimed_leases/sec, and reconciliation errors.
Migration: old surge-pool code paths remain behind feature flag until canary validated.
Data retention: lease history kept for 90 days to aid billing disputes and incident investigations.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: use time-decay leases rather than pre-allocated credits. Rationale: simpler realtime reclamation and lower memory footprint. Tradeoff: slightly more noisy accounting vs discrete credits.

Decision: smoothing_window default 1 hour instead of 24h. Rationale: minimizes customer surprise while keeping billing signal timely. Tradeoff: short smoothing window can still cause charge spikes for very bursty tenants.

Decision: autoscaler fast-path allowed only when node provisioning latency < configured threshold to avoid long provisioning leading to runaway bill. Tradeoff: less aggressive scale-up on slow regions.
Open question: whether to expose tenant-configurable burst-pricing tiers vs single standard model. Proposed: surface recommended tiers in Console and default to standard for initial launch.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Unit + integration tests. Deploy feature-flagged binary to staging compute clusters.
Phase 1: Canary with 5 internal tenants (Rina + SE sandbox). Monitor p95 latency, pool utilization, billing events for 72h.
Phase 2: Expand to 50 customers with opt-in flag in Console. Collect feedback and watch for invoice disputes.
Phase 3: Gradual opt-out removal and enable-by-default for new Dedicated tenants. Post-launch: 30-day metrics evaluation window and one patch release for fixes.
Rollback triggers: >5% increase in p95 latency for any affected tenant, >2 unexplained billing disputes within 24h, or >10% increase in global error rate.
test_plan: Load tests: synthetic spike patterns (10s–5m bursts) across 3 different request distributions to measure lease grant/trim behavior
Chaos tests: simulate node provisioning delays and forced pool shortages to validate reclamation and autoscaler interactions
Billing tests: end-to-end pipeline from soft_commit_event to invoice line generation with smoothing_window boundary tests
SLO regression tests: ensure no statistically significant p95 degradation for baseline tenants during canary
Integration tests for Console UI showing predictive cost estimates matching simulated billing output

2026-02-28 Product review: PM Lina Chen requested Console forecasting widget and an email digest when tenant uses >70% of monthly burst budget.
